''27. Worke not the meate.''] By their greedy {{ls}}eeking after him for meate of the body, he taketh occa{{ls}}ion to dravv them to the de{{ls}}ire of a more excellent foode which he had to giue them, and {{ls}}o by litle to open vnto them the great meate and my{{ls}}terie of the B. Sacrament: which (as he proueth) doth not onely far pa{{ls}}{{ls}}e their ordinarie bread or his maruelous multiplied loaues, but Manna it {{ls}}elf, which they thought came from heauen, and {{ls}}o much wondered at it.

''32. The true bread.''] Though the per{{ls}}on of Chri{{ls}}t incarnate, euen out of the Sacrament al{{ls}}o, be meant vnder the Metaphores of bread and drinke from heauen: and our beleefe in him, be {{ls}}ignified by eating and feeding: yet the cau{{ls}}es why they {{ls}}hould be recommended vnto vs in {{ls}}uch termes, were, that he was to be eaten and drunken in deed in the formes of bread and wine: for the which cau{{ls}}e his body on the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e is called {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Why Chri{{ls}}t is called bread: & beleeuing, eating.}}his bread: & his bloud {{ls}}hed on the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ierem. 11, 19. Gen. 49, 11''.}}the bloud of the grape: no doubt becau{{ls}}e the {{ls}}ame body and bloud were in Holy Sacrament to be eaten and drunken. In which {{ls}}peaches, either of Chri{{ls}}ts per{{ls}}on generally, or peculiarly of the {{ls}}ame as in the B. Sacrament, ''the true bread'' is not taken proprely and {{ls}}pecially for that {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance which is of corne, and called with vs bread: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=What {{ls}}ignifieth, The true bread.}}but generally for food or meate, and therfore it hath ioyned vvith it lightly a terme {{ls}}ignifying a more excellent {{ls}}ort of {{ls}}u{{ls}}tenance: as, the true bread, the bread of heauen, the bread of life, Super{{ls}}ub{{ls}}tantial bread. in which {{ls}}ort the holy Sacrament which is Chri{{ls}}ts body, is both here, and in S. Luke and S. Paul al{{ls}}o, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 2, 42. 20, 7''.}}often called bread, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The B. Sacrament called bread.}}euen after con{{ls}}ecration: not onely for that it was made of bread, but becau{{ls}}e it is bread more truely, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1 Cor. 10''.}}and by more excellent property and calling, then that vvhich ordinarily is named bread.

''44. Dravv him.''] The Father dravveth vs and teacheth vs to come to his Sonne, and to beleeue the{{ls}}e high and hard my{{ls}}teries of his incarnation and of feeding vs vvith his ovvne {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance in the Sacrament: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Aug. cont. duas Ep. Pelag. li. 1 c. 19. & Ser. 2 de verb. Ap. c. 2''.}}{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=God draweth vs with our free wil.}}not compelling or violenty forcing any again{{ls}}t their will or without any re{{ls}}pect of their con{{ls}}ent, as Heretikes pretend: but by the {{ls}}weete internal motions and per{{ls}}ua{{ls}}ions of his grace and {{ls}}pirit he wholy maketh vs of our owne will and liking to con{{ls}}ent to the {{ls}}ame.

''49. Manna, and died.''] The Heretikes holding the fathers of the old Te{{ls}}tament to haue eaten of the {{ls}}ame meate, and to haue had as good Sacraments as we, be here refuted: Chri{{ls}}t putting a plaine difference in the very {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance thereof, and in the graces and effects much more at large. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The manifold preeminences of the B. Sacrament aboue Manna.}}Manna was onely a figure of the B. Sacrament, though a very excellent figure thereof for many cau{{ls}}es. It came in a {{ls}}ort from heauen, our Sacrament more: it vvas made by God miraculou{{ls}}ly, our Sacrament more: it was to be eaten for the time of their peregrination, our Sacrament more: it was to euery man what he liked be{{ls}}t, our Sacrament more: a litle thereof {{ls}}erued and {{ls}}ufficed as wel as much, our Sacrament more: it vvas re{{ls}}erued for {{ls}}uch daies as it could not be gathered, and our Sacrament much more: it vvas kept for a memorial in the arke of the Te{{ls}}tament, our Sacrament much more: the di{{ls}}contented and incredulous murmured and gain{{ls}}aid it, at our Sacrament much more: it {{ls}}u{{ls}}tained their bodies in the de{{ls}}ert, our Sacrament both body and {{ls}}oule much more.

''52. Hovv can this man.''] ''It came not to their minde that nothing was impo{{ls}}sible to God, that wickedly {{ls}}aid, Hovv can this man giue vs his fle{{ls}}h? but vve may make great profite of their {{ls}}inne, beleeuing the My{{ls}}teries, and taking a le{{ls}}{{ls}}on, neuer to {{ls}}ay or once thinke, Hovv? for it is a Iewi{{ls}}h word and worthy al punishment''. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=In the B. Sacrament, ''How'', is a Iewi{{ls}}h word.}}{{ls}}o {{ls}}aith ''S. Cyril. li. 4 c. 13 in Io''. Neuertheles if one a{{ls}}ked onely for de{{ls}}ire to learne in humility, as our Lady did touching her hauing a childe in her virginitie, then he mu{{ls}}t take the Angels an{{ls}}wer to her, That it is of the Holy Gho{{ls}}t. {{ls}}o {{ls}}aith S. Dama{{ls}}cene ''li. 4. c. 14''.

''53. vnles you eate.'') ''Chri{{ls}}t commending the Sacrament of the faithful vnto vs, {{ls}}aid, Except you eate &c. you can not haue life in you. So the life {{ls}}aith of life, and to him that thinketh the life to be a lier, this meate {{ls}}hal be death & not life to him''. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The real pre{{ls}}ence.}}Augu{{ls}}t. ''Ser. 2 de verb. Ap. c. 1''. And S. Leo thus, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ser. 6 de ieiun. 7. mens''.}}''Becau{{ls}}e our Lord {{ls}}aith, Except you eate &c. let vs {{ls}}o communicate that vve nothing doubt of the truth of Chri{{ls}}tes body and bloud: for that is receiued vvith mouth, vvhich is beleeued in hart: and they an{{ls}}vver Amen in vaine, that di{{ls}}pute again{{ls}}t that vvhich they receiue''.

''53. And drinke.'') This the Prote{{ls}}tants alleage for the nece{{ls}}sitie of receiuing in both kindes: but in re{{ls}}pect of them {{ls}}elues (who lightly hold al this chapter to pertaine nothing to the Sacramental receiuing, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Receiuing in both kindes not nece{{ls}}sarie.}}but to {{ls}}piritual feeding on Chri{{ls}}t by faith onely) it can make nothing for one kinde or other. And in re{{ls}}pect of vs Catholikes, who beleeue Chri{{ls}}ts whole per{{ls}}on both humanitie and Diuinitie, both fle{{ls}}h and bloud to be in either forme, and to be wholy receiued no le{{ls}}{{ls}}e in the fir{{ls}}t, then in the {{ls}}econd or in both, this place commaundeth nothing for both the kindes.

''53. You {{ls}}hal not haue life.'') Though the Catholikes teach the{{ls}}e wordes to be {{ls}}poken of the Sacrament, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Sacramental receiuing of Chri{{ls}}ts body, not alwaies nece{{ls}}sarie to {{ls}}aluation.}}yet they meane not (no more then our Sauiour here doth) to exclude al from {{ls}}aluation, that receiue not actually and Sacramentally vnder one or both kindes. For then children that die after they be baptized and neuer receiued Sacramentally, {{ls}}hould peri{{ls}}h: which to hold, were heretical Neither did S. Augu{{ls}}tine meane, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Li. 1 de pec. merit. c. 20''}}applying the{{ls}}e wordes to infants al{{ls}}o, that they could not be {{ls}}aued without receiuing {{ls}}acramentally; as not onely the Heretikes, but Era{{ls}}mus did {{hws|vnlear|vnlearnedly}}<noinclude>{{rh|||nedly}}</noinclude>
